ticket.title: the suite view is a snapshot rather than a projection, so root reads serve stale member status and deleting the index changes the answer
ticket.description:
Measured 2026-11-10 while closing SP-50, and it is why the board numbers in this session flip-flopped between two shapes. The root index (.gaugeblock/storypole/index.sqlite) held 374 task rows - a materialised copy of the whole suite - while storypole own index held 49 and the suite view answered 106 active. SP-50 was verified and archived in the storypole store, storypole show SP-50 in that store said Verified, and the root answered in_progress for the same ticket because its copy predates the verification. SP-47 and SP-49 read correctly in both, so the copy is refreshed by something that did not run after SP-50. Three measurements: (1) deleting workspace.sqlite changed nothing - the list still answered 106 rows with SP-50 in_progress, so the stale row is in index.sqlite; (2) deleting index.sqlite dropped the answer to 65 rows with SP-50 absent entirely, so the suite view is a snapshot rather than a projection rebuilt on read; (3) storypole ledger-reconcile reports index and ledger agree throughout, because it compares the root store own tasks and is blind to copied member rows. That falsifies the invariant SP-36 states - deleting index.sqlite changes no answer - for the suite view specifically. Consequence for the burn-down: every status read from the root may be stale by up to one rollup, so the owning repository is the only trustworthy reader, which is the opposite of what a meta-harness is for. Wanted: the suite view rebuilds from member records on read or on demand, a refresh verb that can be shown to converge, and reconcile extended to copied rows so a stale one is reported rather than agreed with. Acceptance: verifying a member ticket is visible from the root immediately, deleting either index file changes no answer, and reconcile names any row whose copy disagrees with its owner.

FIXED 2026-11-10 (storypole 2219cd6), in two halves, because either alone was wrong. Purge: a rebuild records how many tasks it produced and opening compares that with the live row count, so foreign or missing rows force a rebuild - the marker is the rebuild task count, not the record-file count, because a record file can carry events without naming a task and the file count would rebuild on every command. Route: list at a suite root reads the workspace rollup, which replays every member records on open, instead of that store own index. Measured after installing the fixed binary: the root index fell from 374 rows to 65 (its own), the suite view answered 106 rows with SP-50 absent and no in_progress row, and list at the root costs 1.8 s wall (0.29 user, 0.34 sys) against an instant stale cache - that is the price of replaying twelve stores and it is stated rather than assumed. Records mode only: all twelve stores are records mode (common carries a legacy ledger beside its tickets directory and records win), so the legacy ledger index keeps its old behaviour deliberately. Tests: index_ownership_tests pins that a foreign row is purged on reopen and that deleting the index changes no answer; nextest -p storypole-core 180 passed.

CORRECTION to the numbers in the paragraph above, measured rather than restated: the root index now holds 173 rows, and 65 is what list reports after excluding archived tickets - the pre-fix file held 374, so 201 member rows were purged, not 309. What stands is the composition: zero rows with a member prefix (SP-, MTR-, BW-, OF-, RB-, CO-, CH-, JN-, SH-) remain in the root index, list answers 106 rows with SP-50 absent, and the same command from inside storypole still answers for that repository alone. The 1.8 s figure is unchanged and is the cost of the routing half.
